evidence:
The actual frozen root workbook and bundled workbook were opened with openpyxl. In both, Quality Checks!row 21 (number 20) says: "The reference is a committed, static baseline ? not regenerated, fetched, or nondeterministic on any pinned value." Internal Quality Checks!row 21 agrees. The frozen skill references/quality-checks.md:87-88 requires a committed baseline, reproducible seed rows, and no variable source for graded fixed figures. This is a pinned-value requirement, not a ban on execution-security tokens or elapsed-time measurement. Deterministic Checks!rows 12 and 34 (fixtures and solve contract), references/deterministic-checks.md:62, and staged-task-contract.md:15-17,175-176 were applied manually for this row's relevant source/seed/deployment aspects; no private checker run is claimed.

All 50 task files and all 34 frozen rule/template files independently matched the SHA256 entries in qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/manifest.json. All 23 solution files are tracked and match git HEAD after line-ending normalization; 20 match byte-for-byte, while src/style.css, src/vendor.js and public/assets/index-C_1hOHr1.css differ from the git blob only in CRLF/LF. The solution git status was clean. Thus this is committed source and compiled output, not an untracked regenerated baseline. solution/solve.sh:25-26 removes the deployment's old database files and executes only `cp -a "$source_app/." /app/`; it contains no build, package install, generator, network retrieval or model call. solution/app/public/index.html:1-2 references shipped JS/CSS. package.json:14-19 pins declared package versions, and the lockfile and vendored/built frontend bytes are included in the verified manifest.

The baseline data is explicitly empty: environment/assets/seed_data.json:3 is `"snippets": []`. server.js:113-128 creates an empty SQLite schema using CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and does not insert seed records or fetch data. Saved identities are SQLite INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT (server.js:119), and revisions start at 1 and increment only on successful writes (server.js:72,84). No random seed ID, date-dependent seed row, downloaded fixture or remote boot-time data source exists. All five executable examples were read: hello.js:4-8 deterministically prints squares 1 through 12 and logs the count; counter.html starts at zero; sheet.css is literal CSS; broken.js and slow.js are fixed intentional failure examples. Startup app.tsx:143-144 loads the existing local library, or this committed hello.js on an empty library. Its fetch('/starters/' + name) at app.tsx:56 is local delivery of the static directory mapped by server.js:100, not retrieval of a changing external reference.

Every task-authored randomness/time hit was traced. runtime.ts:127-128 creates guard names and CSP nonces; :145 creates handler-selector tokens; :181 creates the active preview token; :192 checks that token and event source. Snapshot code :68-70 removes scripts/meta and data-cw handler attributes. app.tsx:42 uses a UUID only as a React console-row key, which :166 does not display as a scored value. The executed built JS contains the same paths at public/assets/index-VduTT3aN.js:28792-28793,28815-28818,28890,28919,29019; framework random keys and editing-event clocks also do not supply baseline data. These are ephemeral execution identifiers, not saved snippet identities or pinned expected content. server.js:73,85 writes the actual wall-clock updated_at only when the user creates/changes a record. No criterion fixes an absolute timestamp; functional/prompt.md:13,19 requires observing actual identities/revisions and :363-366 compares saved data against its recorded pre-restart state. Duration is deliberately measured with performance.now (runtime.ts:37-48,79,90), as behaviour.md:19 requests and functional/prompt.md:326 assesses; there is no graded calendar/absolute-date business rule requiring a fixed scenario date.

Raw evidence was inspected, not just the aggregate passed flag. For BOTH golden/run-golden-20260930-070305/RESULTS.json and golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json, all 22 actual_app_files hashes match this snapshot and every recorded driver hash matches its retained driver file. Their facts['S01.startup_ready'].evidence.value has identical title hello, filename hello.js, full committed source, preview squares ending '12 squared is 144', and log text 'printed %d rows' plus 12, with manual_run_used=false. Measured durations differ legitimately: 7.1 ms versus 6.0 ms. The executed workspace_flow.cjs:45-50 opens the app, awaits completion, and reads the fields/body/logs/status before any manual Run. The later raw run's facts['S01.example_separate'] records the original built-in source unchanged after saving its edited copy, and facts['S22.process_restart_durability'] records the same four complete saved records, identities and revisions before/after the actual restart, including unchanged stored timestamps. These corroborate this row's static baseline and stable values; neither run is represented as a full configured judge/Oracle/model run, and their timing does not establish judge workload. No corresponding broader clearance is inferred.
counterexample: False-fail witness actually present: the two hash-matching golden startup observations have identical seeded/example content but durations 7.1 ms and 6.0 ms, while source creates fresh CSP/message UUIDs. Treating any UUID or elapsed-time variation as row-20 failure would reject this conforming reference although no pinned value changes. A valid alternative may also use random identifiers for newly created user records if the identities persist and the judge records their actual values; they are not preseeded pinned IDs. Broken false-pass challenge (analytical only, no prohibited mutation/run): a static server file could fetch changing starter source at boot or insert a Date.now-derived seed title, and a single startup pass/hash check would not prove row 20. Here the complete solve/server/startup/example paths were checked: the server performs no such fetch/insertion and serves only committed local starter bytes. No actual false-pass witness was found in this candidate.
